punchline: The man who wrote a bestseller on focus has never had a social media account, and his career is the proof he didn't need one.
thirty_sec: Cal Newport, author of Deep Work and a Georgetown computer science professor, has never had a social media account. He still built an academic career and a wide readership. His reasoning: most of us adopt tools because they offer some possible benefit. He calls that the any-benefit approach. A craftsman works differently. First name what really drives your success, then keep a tool only if its upside for those things far outweighs what it costs your attention.
question: If your most-used app had to justify itself against your top goals before you could reinstall it, would it make the cut?
